Commentary: Asitha Fernando to Arafat Minhas, SIX, back to back sixes! They are just one hit away from sealing it. This is higher, longer and better than the previous delivery. Asitha is not nailing those yorkers and is paying the price. Minhas gets under the length and launches it over long-on

Asitha Fernando to Arafat Minhas, FOUR, smashed! Pakistan are almost there. This is exceptional hitting from Minhas. He's been helped by Asitha ofcourse - full toss outside off, Minhas hammers it straight down the ground, with mid-off inside the ring, there's no need to run for that
Asitha Fernando to Arafat Minhas, THATS OUT!! Caught&Bowled!!

Asitha Fernando to Arafat Minhas, out Caught&Bowled!! Oh no! Minhas won't be there to see Pakistan over the line. But he's done his part. A 31-ball 61 when the team needed, take a bow! Asitha goes short and into the pitch, Minhas is backing away and is rushed on the pull, the ball hits the splice of the bat and lobs towards cover. Asitha runs across and takes a good catch. Arafat Minhas c and b Asitha Fernando 61(31) [4s-3 6s-4]
Faheem Ashraf, left handed bat, comes to the crease
Asitha Fernando to Faheem Ashraf, THATS OUT!! Caught!!

Asitha Fernando to Faheem Ashraf, out Caught by Maheesh Theekshana!! Faheem goes for a duck. Asitha is on a hat-trick. Finally a catch is taken at third man. Short and outside off, Faheem tries to ramp it over third man but does not get enough to clear the rope. Theekshana runs to his left and takes it safely. Faheem Ashraf c Maheesh Theekshana b Asitha Fernando 0(1)
Shaheen Afridi, left handed bat, comes to the crease
Asitha Fernando to Shaheen Afridi, no run, 136.1ks full and at the stumps, Shaheen eases it to mid-on
Dilshan Madushanka to Hasan Nawaz, 1 run, 131.9ks short of length delivery, Nawaz rides the bounce and steers to backward point
Dilshan Madushanka to Shaheen Afridi, no run, 131.1ks bouncer angling in, Shaheen tries to take it on but the ball climbs over the top-edge

Dilshan Madushanka to Shaheen Afridi, SIX, Pakistan win by 3 wickets. The skipper finishes it off in style. If there were roofs in the Gaddafi Stadium then it would be coming down right now - that's how loud the noise is. This is the joint highest chase in an ODI final, level with that India v England game at Lord's in 2002. Another short of length delivery from Madushanka, but he didn't get the bounce as the previous delivery, Shaheen rocks back and nails the pull over deep mid-wicket

Fakhar Zaman | Player of the Match (1/2) - [On his knock] Look, the way my first four matches had gone, I felt a good performance was due, and I was putting in the effort. But cricket is such a game that sometimes you're in really good touch, but the runs just don't come. Even today, I was struggling a little at the start, but luckily the runs came, and that's a good thing for me. Whenever there is a final, I seem to score runs. [On the partnership with Saad Baig after Pakistan lost two early wickets] I've played domestic cricket with him as well, and he's a very talented player. Even today, when I was struggling at that stage, he came in and scored quite quickly. That allowed me to relax and take my time. If he had also played slowly like me, perhaps I would have tried to take a few more chances, and if you take those chances, you can end up losing your wicket. So the credit goes to him for the way he started and the way he built his innings. In my opinion, his was the best innings of the match.

Arafat Minhas  | Player of the Series (1/2) - [On his bowling improvement and his batting contributions] Absolutely. Just as the team needed today. When I went in, we were talking about belief, that we had to believe in each other. And I think that belief was there. We enjoyed those moments in the middle, and we won the match. [On staying calm and executing his skills under pressure] Yes, absolutely, there is pressure. I think the more you enjoy that pressure, the calmer you remain and the better you execute your skills. That was exactly what I tried to do, to stay calm in the middle. Both of us knew each other's abilities, so we were playing after calculating things, and that's what helped us win the match.

Arafat Minhas (2/2): [On how they assessed Sri Lanka's bowling options and capitalised on an opportunity towards the end] Absolutely, we had an idea. Even when from outside (dugout), we had been told that they might have a bit of an issue with their overs because their frontline bowlers had already bowled a lot. We were calculating that and playing accordingly. And towards the end, when I got the opportunity, I charged and got a really good big over. So I think we were playing with that kind of calculation, and we took the game right till the end. [On his identity as an all-rounder and his commitment to contributing in both departments] Absolutely, winning a final brings its own happiness. And I think I've been saying from the beginning that I am an all-rounder, and I always try to give 100 per cent with both my batting and bowling.
